question: Which of the following social reformers is credited with the establishment of ‘Bharat Stree Mahamandal’ in 1910?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarala Devi Chaudhurani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarala Devi Chaudhurani:**

 
 
• Sarala Devi Chaudhurani (1872-1945) was an Indian nationalist and social reformer.
 
• She founded the Bharat Stree Mahamandal in 1910, one of the earliest women's organizations in India.
 
• The organization aimed to promote women's education and empowerment.
 
• She advocated for women's participation in national life and social reform.
 
• She was also a musician, writer, and political activist.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarojini Naidu:**

 
 
• Sarojini Naidu (1879-1949) was an Indian political activist, poet, and feminist.
 
• She was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• She was the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress
 
• She also served as the Governor of Uttar Pradesh.She was known as the "Nightingale of India" for her poetry.
 
 
 
• **Usha Mehta:**
 
 
• Usha Mehta (1920-2000) was an Indian freedom fighter.
 
• She is remembered for organizing the "Secret Congress Radio" during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
 
• This underground radio broadcasted nationalist messages and news during the movement.
 
• She played a crucial role in disseminating information and maintaining morale during a critical period of the independence struggle.
 
• She was a strong advocate of Gandhian principles.
 
 
 
• **Savitri Bai Phule:**
 
 
• Savitri Bai Phule (1831-1897) was an Indian social reformer, educationalist, and poet.
 
• She is considered India's first female teacher.
 
• She, along with her husband Jyotirao Phule, played a vital role in advancing women's education in India.
 
• They founded the first girls' school in Pune in 1848.
 
• She fought against caste and gender discrimination.
